newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore visitor arrivals down 5.9 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Singapore visitor arrivals down 5.9 pct in Sept.

text.p: Visitor arrivals in Singapore fell 5.9 percent in September compared with the same month last year, state television reported on Tuesday, quoting the Singapore Tourist Promotion Board (STPB).
The STPB said it was the third consecutive month the overall number had fallen.
Visitors from Japan, Singapore's single largest market, were down 6.7 percent from last September -- the fifth consecutive month the number of arrivals from Japan has dropped.
The STPB said Japanese tourists were heading instead to Hong Kong ahead of the British colony's handover to China in mid-1997.

But the STPB added overall growth in the first nine months of the year was 1.5 percent higher than in the same period in 1995. It also said that preliminary figures for October showed growth of about two percent compared with October last year.
